notes: On their own turn, bots now weigh the attack a player who has been hitting them can make next, so they are less likely to tap out or clear the board and then take a big swing.
Bots now wait until blockers are declared before using an instant-speed pump such as Giant Growth.
Bots now play their lands and mana toward casting their commander a turn sooner, such as cracking Krosan Verge for the colours The First Sliver needs.
Bots now attack with a menace creature when the defender has only one creature to block it, and equip menace to finish a player with commander damage.
Bots no longer spend Umezawa's Jitte's counters on a pump that can't help them, such as on a creature about to be handed to an opponent.
201 more cards are playable, among them Juxtapose, Chorus of the Conclave, Spy Kit, Shaman's Trance, Time and Tide and Okk.
Journey to Eternity, Radiant Grace and Skin Invasion no longer come back when they were exiled instead of going to the graveyard.
An attacker that is already blocked no longer becomes blocked again when an effect adds another blocker, so its "whenever it becomes blocked" abilities don't trigger twice.
When more than one card changes what a land's mana becomes (Naked Singularity beside Reality Twist), the player tapping it now picks among them, instead of only the newest applying.
In multiplayer, False Orders can now take a blocker controlled by any of the attacking player's opponents.
Bots no longer cast Gamble when it's their only card, since its random discard could only throw away the card it found.
Bots stop aiming more pings at a creature once the ones already on the stack will kill it.
Bots keep a redirecting spell such as Deflecting Swat until there is a spell or ability worth turning aside.
69 more cards are playable, among them Lightning Storm, Mob Mentality, Soulflayer, Piracy, Land Equilibrium and Kaervek's Torch.
A commander that mutates onto another creature, or melds, stays your commander: when it leaves, its card can go back to the command zone, and its combat damage still counts as commander damage.
When one trigger goes on the stack twice at once (Delney, Streetwise Lookout), the history now says so (×2), so every hit it makes is accounted for.

Bots no longer cast a discovered spell that can only fizzle (Deflecting Swat aimed at the discover itself), and decline a cascaded or discovered spell that would only hurt them, such as Pyroclasm on their own board.
A bot's Clone or Phantasmal Image copies its own Etali, Primal Conqueror for another round of free spells instead of a lesser creature.
Bots no longer cast Mox Diamond with no land to discard, or Backdraft when no opponent has cast a sorcery this turn.
Four new Bracket 4 decks to play against: averages of real Bracket 4 decks for Grand Arbiter Augustin IV, Etali, Primal Conqueror, Zur the Enchanter and Liesa, Shroud of Dusk.
Bots wait to use instant-speed spells and abilities until the moment they matter, instead of firing them off as soon as they can.
Bots no longer cast a counterspell just to set off a trigger of their own, such as Y'shtola's.
Each player's latest choice (a mode, a colour, a creature type, a card named) shows beside their name, through the turn after it was made.
Bots under Fatespinner no longer skip their own main phase with lands and spells in hand, and pick the same step again for a second Fatespinner.
Bots treat putting a permanent into its owner's library as removal: Wan Shi Tong, All-Knowing now aims at an opponent's permanent and gets cast.
Bots no longer make token copies of their own legendary creatures, which died to the legend rule at once (Echocasting Symposium).
Bots use Jace, Multiverse Architect's −3 when it's the better play.
A game no longer stops with an error at the end step after a token copy of Avacyn, Angel of Horror dies.
While deciding on a mulligan, the card under your mouse grows so you can read it, as cards in your hand do.
In a two-seat lobby, a bot can be taken out again, leaving its seat open.
Adding a bot, the deck list opens on the tab you last looked at.
The site now tells you when a new version is out, and this page lists what changed in each one.
"Order my triggers" stays on after you take a turn back.
A token copy goes to the player whose effect made it, even when the original has changed hands (Preston, the Vanisher; Spitting Image).
The graveyard and exile buttons glow while you can cast, play or activate something from there.
Delayed abilities and effects that last a while are listed beside a player's emblems.
A card everyone saw go into a hand stays face up for everyone.
The modes chosen for a spell are shown to the whole table, a permanent shows whose it is when owner and controller differ, and one that taps for an ability shows a tap symbol.
